tools.name: list_patterns
tools.description: List Motion Menu patterns. Every row is "number  slug  <role>  [tags]  · title". ROLE is where the pattern goes on a page (hero, nav, pricing, background, product, form…) — filter by it when you are building a page rather than hunting an effect. The SLUG is the permanent identity — prefer it. Filter

tools.name: get_pattern
tools.description: Get one pattern by number, including its complete transplantable HTML, CSS and JS. Pass framework to get a ready-to-use component wrapper (react .tsx, vue .vue, svelte .svelte, or vanilla .ts). Pass theme (e.g. "daf", "wb", "blmedia" — see list_themes) to receive the bundle ALREADY re-skinned: theme

tools.name: list_themes
tools.description: List available Motion Menu themes (name, mode, label) for get_pattern/get_theme.

tools.name: get_theme
tools.description: Get one theme: token values, font stacks, ready-to-paste :root CSS block, and the literal→color substitution map for theming code by hand (exact strings: hex, 0x numbers, "r,g,b" triplets, GLSL vec3). Build/tune themes at /theme.html.

tools.name: compose_page
tools.description: Compose a complete standalone working page from Motion Menu patterns — OR, given a `brief` instead of `sections`, get back a structured COMPOSITION PLAN (pattern picks with reasons, no HTML) reasoned over the pattern graph: role fit, pairs_with affinity, clashes checked across the whole plan, max_pe

tools.name: get_kit
tools.description: Get the Motion Menu build kit: the design laws, the one-page act protocol, stack pins, known gotchas, and the full pattern index. Call this FIRST before building a page.

tools.name: get_design_digest
tools.description: Get the machine-readable Motion Menu quality contract. Call before build_page or compose_page. It defines anti-generic composition rules, motion lifecycle, responsive requirements, truth constraints, and release verification gates.

tools.name: check_updates
tools.description: Check whether patterns you already built with have changed. findings.detail: Tool "recommend_patterns" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.
